facts.raw_span: episodes of spasms and tremors in her right hand and forearm
underwent carpal tunnel release surgery initially
tremors recurred
progressive right-sided weakness, dysarthria, hand tremors, slurred speech, and gait instability
No specific physical examination findings were reported in the case

T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery MRI showed hyperintensities throughout the bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter, corpus callosum, basal ganglia, thalami, midbrain, upper pons, and middle cerebellar peduncles
T1-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery MRI with contrast showed absence of contrast enhancement
Brain Biopsy (left frontal lesion): CD5− CD10− CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ EBV/EBER−
Cytogenetic study: Normal female karyotype
Fluorescence in situ hybridization: Extra copies of BCL6 (3q27) and BCL2 (18q21), no MYC abnormalities
Cerebrospinal fluid: Presence of lymphoma cells
Bone marrow: Negative for lymphoma cells

concepts.why: The presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid and the brain biopsy results, along with the characteristic imaging findings of hyperintensities on T2-weighted MRI and absence of contrast enhancement, support this diagnosis.
The brain biopsy results showing CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ and extra copies of BCL6 and BCL2, along with the presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid, are consistent with this diagnosis.
The negative bone marrow biopsy for lymphoma cells suggests that the lymphoma may have originated from a different site and spread to the CNS.

rationales.F04: Progressive neurological symptoms suggest a primary CNS process.
rationales.F06: Extensive non-enhancing lesions are characteristic of primary CNS lymphoma.
rationales.F07: Absence of contrast enhancement is typical of primary CNS lymphoma.
rationales.F08: Brain biopsy showing CD20+ B cells is diagnostic of lymphoma.
rationales.F10: Extra copies of BCL6 and BCL2 are common in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
rationales.F11: Presence of lymphoma cells in cerebrospinal fluid confirms CNS involvement.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid, brain biopsy results, and extensive nonenhancing lesions in the bilateral cerebral hemispheres support the diagnosis of Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma, which is a type of lymphoma that originates in the brain.
